overview: This single-page file consists of a list-of-papers cover sheet for a communication concerning military aviation in Japanese-ruled Taiwan. It records a June 27 item sent from Taihoku to the U.S. Embassy in Tokyo, reporting the selection of a site on the outskirts of Kagi for an army aviation field and noting plans for hangars, workshops, and barracks for an aviation regiment; the communication apparently enclosed three articles from the Taiwanese press.

subfiles.summary: The cover sheet identifies one communication from Taihoku to the U.S. Embassy in Tokyo, dated June 27, although no year is given. It reports that a site on the outskirts of Kagi had been selected for an army aviation field and that hangars, workshops, and barracks would be erected to accommodate an aviation regiment. The underlying communication enclosed three newspaper articles from the Taiwanese press, but those articles are not present in the supplied OCR text.

interest: The page is useful as evidence of Japanese military aviation infrastructure development in colonial Taiwan and of American diplomatic monitoring of that development through the local press. Its reference to three enclosed newspaper articles indicates a larger evidentiary packet that is not represented in the surviving OCR supplied here. The planned combination of hangars, workshops, barracks, and a resident aviation regiment suggests a substantial operational base rather than a simple landing ground.
